To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Ritual and ceremony in the intraoperative MRI suite is a complex process involving many participants and many elements.
the non-quantitative elements of healing are not unique to shamanic and other traditional healing practices but are also found in modern clinical settings.
The non-medical activities of the caregivers and the patient in an iMRI assisted brain operation were found to be similar to those of traditional and shamanistic healers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we can best use the iMRI technology and the healing process to best advantage for the patient.
the identification of nonmedical factors in the healing encounter.
the visual documentation of non-quantifiable aspects of the healing encounter that may be overlooked in the rush to quantify and measure the effectiveness of medical interventions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the iMRI assisted brain operation is a ritual of intention.
the iMRI surgical procedure is a healing ritual that is not only a medical procedure but also a culturally determined healing encounter that is a part of a broader healing process.
the rituals and ceremony of the iMRI assisted brain surgical encounter are a form of healing art.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are all healers and we all heal.
the healing encounter is a complex interaction between the caregiver and the patient and that the healing process is an interaction between the patient and the environment.
the patient and caregivers were engaged in the healing process through ritual and ceremony, in the context of an intraoperative MRI assisted surgery, which is not a traditional practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can learn from other healing practices to improve our own.
the healing process is not limited to medical interventions, but also involves a number of other non medical activities that can be identified and studied.
we can use our artistic skills to observe and analyze non-quantifiable elements of healing and that this can be a powerful way to understand how to better engage patients in the healing process.
